description.html: The castle with a gate is a decoration shaped like an old fortress with two square battlemented towers joined by a wall with a large arched gate. The stone surfaces have pronounced brick and window details, and the moss on the walls gives the impression of a building that has stood underwater for a long time.

The wide gate is a real passage: fish swim through it freely, so the castle is not just an ornament but part of their route through the aquarium. It looks best in the middle of the setup or against the back glass, where the gate stands out. The towers and windows complete the look of a medieval castle, and the green details tie it to the plants.

Before placing it, rinse the castle in lukewarm water, without detergents. Set it on a flat surface so the passage under the gate stays open and sand does not fill it. If you place it against the back glass, leave a little space behind it for easier cleaning. Remove algae from the walls and moss with a soft brush during regular maintenance.
